beats.text: When the Oliver family gave up their 38-room mansion in South Bend, they left the furniture behind. Nearly everything stayed.
beats.label: SOUTH BEND, INDIANA

beats.text: The Olivers named the house for the Scottish village James Oliver came from.
beats.label: THE NAME
beats.credit: University of Notre Dame; state historical marker (2024)

beats.text: James Oliver patented his chilled plow in 1857. His South Bend factory grew into one of the largest plow works in the world.
beats.label: THE OLIVER PLOW
beats.credit: Indiana Public Media; American Society of Agricultural and Biological Engineers

beats.text: His son, Joseph, built the mansion of Indiana fieldstone. The family moved in on New Year's Day, 1897.
beats.label: NEW YEAR'S DAY, 1897
beats.credit: The History Museum, South Bend; ABC57

beats.text: Olivers lived there for some 75 years. In 1988, the family gave the house to the local historical society, furnishings and all.
beats.label: ABOUT 75 YEARS
beats.credit: The History Museum, South Bend; ABC57

beats.text: Today it's part of The History Museum, and you can tour the rooms the family left behind.
beats.label: OPEN FOR TOURS
beats.credit: The History Museum, South Bend; Visit South Bend (2025)

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
